patterns.title: Plain present verb said without b- (yebsetu -> byebsetu, akhalli -> bakhalli, adfa3 -> badfa3)
patterns.wrong: yebsetu / yeksaru / khalli / adfa3 / tista3mel / yikoon
patterns.right: byebsetu / byeksaru / bakhalli / badfa3 / btista3mli / bikoon
patterns.wrong_arabic: يبسطوا / يكسروا / خلي / أدفع / تستعمل / يكون
patterns.right_arabic: بيبسطوا / بيكسروا / بخلي / بدفع / بتستعملي / بيكون
patterns.why: In an ordinary present statement (no want/must/lamma/iza before it) he leaves the b- off the verb, and every ordinary present verb starts with b-.
patterns.english: they make (someone) happy / they break / I let / then I pay / you use the phone / it rains

patterns.title: Masculine adjective on a feminine noun (lugha jdeed, khadra mukhtalef, ed-dunya baared, madeena haadi)
patterns.wrong: lugha jdeed / khadra mukhtalef / dunya baared / madeenti haadi
patterns.right: lugha jdeede / khadra mukhtalfe / ed-dunya baarda / madeenti haadye
patterns.wrong_arabic: لغة جديد / خضرا مختلف / دنيا بارد / مدينتي هادي
patterns.right_arabic: لغة جديدة / خضرا مختلفة / الدنيا باردة / مدينتي هادية
patterns.why: When the noun is feminine (lugha, khadra, ed-dunya, madeena) he keeps the adjective masculine, and the adjective should take the feminine -a ending.
patterns.english: a new language / different vegetables / the weather is cold / my city is quiet / a big table

patterns.title: MSA form where her sheet has the Levantine word (maa2 -> mayy, dajaaj -> jaaj, al-aan -> halla, malee2 -> malyaan, tilka -> hadeek)
patterns.why: He says the book (MSA) form of a word he knows in her dialect form, and she lets it pass (the Arabic-script engine may also normalise what he said, so please confirm).
patterns.english: lots of water / chicken / now / my day was a bit full / I forgot that word

patterns.title: kam marra used for 'one more time' (Kam marra -> Kaman marra)
patterns.why: Whenever he wants her to repeat he says kam marra (how many times) instead of kaman marra (one more time), and she just repeats the sentence.
patterns.english: once more? / say that again?

patterns.title: el- on the first word of an idafa (el-awwal mushkile -> awwal mushkile, esh-shamaal Rusya -> shamaal Rusya)
patterns.wrong: el-awwal mushkile / el-awwal el-fe3el / el-awwal matar / esh-shamaal Rusya
patterns.right: awwal mushkile / awwal el-fe3el / awwal matar / shamaal Rusya
patterns.wrong_arabic: الأول مشكلة / الـ أول الـ فعل / الأول مطر / الشمال روسيا
patterns.right_arabic: أول مشكلة / أول الفعل / أول مطر / شمال روسيا
patterns.why: He puts el- on the first word of a possession pair (awwal X, shamaal X), and in idafa the first word never takes el-; only the last one can.
patterns.english: the first problem / the beginning of the verb / the first rain / the north of Russia

patterns.title: b- kept on the verb after lamma / iza (lamma ba3mel -> lamma a3mel, iza ba2dar -> iza a2dar)
patterns.wrong: lamma ba3mel / iza ba2dar / lamma byiseer / iza ba7kilha
patterns.right: lamma a3mel / iza a2dar / lamma yiseer / iza 7akeetlha
patterns.wrong_arabic: لما بأعمل / إذا بقدر / لما بيصير / إذا بحكيلها
patterns.right_arabic: لما أعمل / إذا أقدر / لما يصير / إذا حكيتلها
patterns.why: After lamma and iza he keeps the b- on the verb, and the b- drops after those time words.
patterns.english: when I do something wrong / if I can fix it / when something happens / if I tell her

patterns.title: English word dropped into an Arabic sentence though the word is on her sheet (or, eat, rice, Iranian)
patterns.why: Mid-sentence he switches to the English word although her sheet has it and he has used the Arabic before, and she answers without flagging it.
patterns.english: I don't like to eat sausage / I talked about rice a lot / there are some Iranians in the UAE

patterns.title: Get-form (t-) dropped: tsawwari for tetsawwari, daaya2ti for etdaaya2ti, mshajje3 for mitshajje3
patterns.wrong: ma baddek tsawwari? / min shu daaya2ti? / ana mshajje3
patterns.right: ma baddek tetsawwari? / min shu etdaaya2ti? / ana mitshajje3
patterns.why: For 'be photographed' and 'you got upset' he says the plain verb (you photograph, you upset someone) and drops the t- that makes it happen to the subject; you said ممتاز / yes both times.
patterns.english: Why don't you want to be photographed? / What did you get upset about? / I am motivated (for the lesson)

patterns.title: Singular noun where he means several (el-madeena 7awaleen, dawle zay dawle 3arabiyye, mat3am irani kteer)
patterns.wrong: el-madeena 7awaleen / dawle zay dawle 3arabiyye / mat3am irani kteer / khu66a (three plans)
patterns.right: el-mudun 7awaleen / duwal zay ed-duwal el-3arabiyye / mata3em iraniyye kteer / khu6a6
patterns.wrong_arabic: المدينة حوالين / دولة زي دولة عربية / مطعم إيراني كتير
patterns.right_arabic: المدن حوالين / دول زي الدول العربية / مطاعم إيرانية كتير
patterns.why: He names two or more things (two cities, Qatar and the UAE, many restaurants) but keeps the noun singular, and the noun should be plural.
patterns.english: the cities around / countries like the Arab countries / there are many Iranian restaurants

patterns.title: I-past said as the bare he-form: ana kharab / ana akal -> ana kharrabt / ana akalet
patterns.why: For 'I did X' in the past he says the bare dictionary form (kharab, akal) with no -t ending on the back, and the ending is what says who did it (kharrabt also needs the doubled middle for 'I ruined').
patterns.english: when I talked too much I ruined everything / today I ate

patterns.title: el- missing on a known thing (3arabi falastini, jaw kteer, ma ba7eb fool)
patterns.wrong: 3arabi falastini / jaw kteer / ma ba7eb fool
patterns.right: el-3arabi el-falastini / el-jaw / ma ba7eb el-fool
patterns.wrong_arabic: عربي فلسطيني / جو كتير / ما بحب فول
patterns.right_arabic: العربي الفلسطيني / الجو / ما بحب الفول
patterns.why: He leaves off el- on a thing both of you already know (Palestinian Arabic, the weather, fool in general), and a known thing takes el-.
patterns.english: with Palestinian Arabic / the weather is very (hot) / I don't like fool

patterns.title: yikoon / akoon used for 'is / am / there is' in the plain present (ma yikoon kahrabji, 3ashan yikoon AC, akoon ma3roof)
patterns.wrong: ma yikoon kahrabji / 3ashan yikoon AC / akoon ana ma3roof
patterns.right: mish kahrabji / 3ashan fi AC / ana ma3roof
patterns.wrong_arabic: ما يكون كهربجي / عشان يكون AC / أكون أنا معروف
patterns.right_arabic: مش كهربجي / عشان في AC / أنا معروف
patterns.why: He adds yikoon / akoon to say 'is', 'there is' or 'I am' about a present fact, and Levantine has no 'to be' there: mish for 'is not', fi / 3indi for 'there is', and nothing for 'I am' (yikoon only after lamma/iza or for habits).
patterns.english: he isn't an electrician / because there is AC / I am known for cooking

patterns.title: Clock time as 3ala + bare number (3ala tamanye -> el-saa3a tamanye / 3ala el-saa3a tamanye)
patterns.right: el-saa3a tamanye / el-saa3a tes3a u nuss
patterns.why: For 'at eight' he says 3ala + the bare number with no el-saa3a, and clock time is el-saa3a + the number (her sheet: 3ala elsaa3a wa7de).
patterns.english: I woke up at eight / at nine thirty

patterns.title: 'See you' reply comes out without its prefix (shufik / ma shuftak -> bashufek / mnshufek)
patterns.why: Answering her bshufek at sign-off he says a clipped form with no b-/person prefix, and the set reply is bashufek or mnshufek (both may be the transcriber clipping the first syllable).
patterns.english: see you

patterns.title: Plural / collective noun for ONE thing (el-8uraf -> el-8urfa, es-sajjaad -> es-sajjaade, el-wlaad -> el-walad)
patterns.why: Talking about one thing (one room, one rug, one sick boy) he uses the plural or collective noun; one item takes the singular (a swallowed final -a could give the same transcript, so please confirm).
patterns.english: I ruined the room by mistake / I showed her the rug / the sick boy must stay at home

patterns.title: Masculine you-form to Amal (inta bta3ref -> inti bta3rfi, haket li -> 7akaiti li)
patterns.why: Talking to Amal he uses the masculine you-form (no -i on the present, -t instead of -ti on the past), and she is feminine so the verb needs the -i / -ti ending.
patterns.english: you know (what a nerd is) / what did you say to me?

patterns.title: Plural people with a singular verb (banaat btruu7 -> el-banaat byruu7u, el-wlaad bykoon wlaad -> bykoon walad)
patterns.why: He puts a plural people-word with a singular verb (the girls goes, the boys is boys); we think the verb and noun must match, plural with plural or one boy with a singular verb.
patterns.english: the girls go to the hairdresser

patterns.title: ma + present verb with no b- (ma yi2dar -> ma byi2dar, ma yikhalsu -> ma byikhalsu)
patterns.why: When he negates a present verb with ma he drops the b- too, and ma + present still needs the b- (ma byi2dar).
patterns.english: it can't write Arabic / they don't finish

patterns.title: MSA -tum for you (pl) past (inza3ajtum -> inza3ajtu, inkasartum -> inkasartu)
patterns.why: In the conjugation runs he gives you (pl) past the MSA ending -tum, and Levantine says -tu (like intu fhemtu on her sheet).
patterns.english: you (pl) got annoyed / you (pl) got broken

patterns.title: el- on the noun but not on the adjective (el-akel mufaddal -> el-akel el-mufaddal, el-akel 3arabi -> el-akel el-3arabi)
patterns.why: In 'the favourite food' / 'the Arab food' he puts el- on the noun only, which turns the phrase into a sentence ('the food is Arab'); as a phrase the adjective needs el- too.
patterns.english: the favourite food in the UAE / like Arab food

patterns.title: fi where Levantine uses bi- (niktub fi -> niktub bi-, fi el-lail -> bil-lail)
patterns.why: For 'write in [letters / a language]' and 'at night' he uses fi, and Levantine uses bi- in both (her sheet has billail).
patterns.english: we write in Arabic or English letters / I work better at night

patterns.title: Object ending dropped from the verb (az3ajtu -> az3ajtuh, bashuf -> bashufek)
patterns.why: He leaves the 'him' / 'you' off the verb, and the object rides on the back of the verb as an ending.
patterns.english: you (pl) annoyed him / see you

patterns.title: English word he used that Amal also used in the same stretch (issue, jacket)
patterns.why: He says an English word that is on her sheet, but Amal herself said the same English word moments before or after, so we are not sure she counts it as a slip.
patterns.english: it has to be a really bad issue / we need a jacket

patterns.title: Wrong reply to ya3tiki el-3afye (Allah ywaffqek / 3afya fiki -> Allah y3afiki)
patterns.why: When she closes with ya3tiki el-3afye he answers with another formula or a garbled one, and the set reply on her sheet is Allah y3afiki.
patterns.english: (reply to 'may God give you health')

patterns.title: eish / shnu for 'what' instead of her shu
patterns.why: He says eish (regional) or shnu (Iraqi/Gulf) for 'what', and her word throughout is shu.
patterns.english: but what? we forget what? / what breakfast do you have?

patterns.title: rann + la- instead of 3ala (I called an engineer)
patterns.why: After rann (to call) he used la-, and her sheet fixes the preposition as 3ala.
patterns.english: I called an engineer

patterns.title: Plural noun after 11 and up (etnaash banaat -> tna3sh benet, 3eshreen sajjaad -> 3eshreen sajjaade)
patterns.why: After numbers from 11 up the noun stays singular, but he said banaat (plural) after twelve.
patterns.english: I have twelve female cousins. / more than twenty rugs

patterns.title: el- on the adjective but not on the noun (min usboo3 el-maadi -> min el-usboo3 el-maadi)
patterns.why: In 'last week' he drops el- from the noun but keeps it on the adjective; both need el- (she had just said min el-usboo3 el-maadi).
patterns.english: since last week

patterns.title: mit2akked (sure) where he wants the verb 'make sure' (-> nit2akkad)
patterns.why: He said 'make sure' in English and then used mit2akked (sure, an adjective) instead of the verb nit2akkad / at2akkad.
patterns.english: Make sure that the AI catches all the mistakes.

patterns.title: zakart (I mentioned) for 'I remembered' (-> tzakkaret)
patterns.why: He meant 'I remembered 80 percent' but said zakart (I mentioned); you said 'exactly, excellent', so we are not sure you heard it.
patterns.english: I remembered eighty percent.

patterns.title: b- dropped after enno (enno i7na niktub -> enno i7na bniktub)
patterns.why: After enno he dropped the b- as if enno were a time word, and after enno the b- is kept.
patterns.english: ...that we write in Arabic or English letters

patterns.title: I-form for 'what makes YOU angry' (shu ba3asseb -> min shu bit3assbi)
patterns.why: Turning her question back on her he used the I-form ba3asseb with no min, and asking her needs the you-f form bit3assbi with min.
patterns.english: in general, what makes you angry?

patterns.title: I-form for the he/it-form (bkhawwefna -> bikhawwefna)
patterns.why: For 'it scares us' he said bkhawwefna, which is 'I scare us'; the it-form needs the yi- (bi-) after the b-.
patterns.english: it scares us (to be parents)

patterns.title: Masculine prefix with feminine ending (byinkasri)
patterns.why: Conjugating inkasar for he/she he mixed the masculine bi- prefix with the feminine -i ending, a form that exists for no subject.
patterns.english: he / she gets broken

patterns.title: We-form of inkasar given as bniksir (we break) instead of bninkasir
patterns.why: For 'we get broken' he gave bniksir, which is the we-form of plain kasar ('we break'); the un-verb needs the extra n (bninkasir).
patterns.english: we get broken

patterns.title: huwwe with a feminine verb (huwwe bassatek -> heyye bassatek)
patterns.why: Repeating her fix bassatek he said huwwe with the feminine verb, and the subject of a she-verb is heyye (he had heyye right twice before, so this may be the engine).
patterns.english: she made you happy

patterns.title: you-f past ending on an I-verb (ma fhemti -> ma fhemet)
patterns.why: Meaning 'I didn't understand' he said fhemti, which is the you-feminine ending; the I-form is fhemet.
patterns.english: I didn't understand

patterns.title: Feminine -a not turned to -t before the owner ending (8urfa-k -> 8urfetek)
patterns.why: He sticks the owner ending straight onto 8urfa, and a feminine noun grows a -t before the ending (8urfet-ek, like 8urfet noam).
patterns.english: she messed up your room

patterns.title: Adjective placed before the noun (qalil kalima -> kalimaat qalile)
patterns.why: He put the adjective in front of the noun the English way, and in Arabic the adjective goes after the noun.
patterns.english: a conversation with few words

patterns.title: el- dropped after hadol (hadol ayyam -> hadol el-ayyam)
patterns.why: After hadol he dropped the el- on the noun, and the noun after hada / hadi / hadol keeps its el-.
patterns.english: these days

patterns.title: la instead of ma before a verb (la ba3ref -> ma ba3ref)
patterns.why: He negated the verb with la, and verbs take ma (la is for commands and for plain 'no').
patterns.english: I don't know; do you know Jambalaya?

patterns.title: 'I'm not sure' without mish (ma ba3ref mit2akked -> mish mit2akked)
patterns.why: For 'I'm not sure' he never put mish in front of mit2akked, and a participle / adjective is negated with mish.
patterns.english: I don't know, I'm not sure, but

patterns.title: ma + pronoun for 'you don't have' (ma intum irani -> ma 3andkom irani)
patterns.why: Retrying her ma 3andkom he turned 3andkom into intum, so the 3and is gone and ma sits on a pronoun; 'you don't have' is ma 3andkom.
patterns.english: you don't have Iranian (food)

patterns.title: 'one of the' without min (wa7ad el-wajibaat -> wa7ad min el-wajibaat)
patterns.why: For 'one of the homeworks' he skipped min after wa7ad, and 'one of' needs min.
patterns.english: I forgot one of the homework sentences

patterns.title: mit7ammes + min instead of la- (excited about)
patterns.why: After mit7ammes he used min, and her sheet fixes the preposition as la-.
patterns.english: excited about the possibility

patterns.title: Pronoun said separately after the preposition (min hom -> minhom)
patterns.why: For 'with them' he said the pronoun as a separate word after the preposition, and the person sticks on the end of the preposition (minhom).
patterns.english: with them

patterns.title: Friday said as yoam el-jam3 (-> yoam el-jum3a)
patterns.why: The day name came out as jam3 (plural) instead of el-jum3a; may be a transcript cut.
patterns.english: today is Friday

patterns.title: 7awaalain (surrounding) for 7awaali (approximately)
patterns.why: For 'about eighteen' he used 7awaalain, and her sheet separates 7awaali (approximately) from 7awaalain (surrounding).
patterns.english: the temperature is around eighteen

patterns.title: MSA ya2ti (comes) for 'it brings us' (-> yjeeblna)
patterns.why: For 'it will bring us the translation' he used MSA ya2ti, and Levantine uses jaab / bijeeb.
patterns.english: it will bring us the translation

patterns.title: sot taweel (long voice) for sot 3aali (loud)
patterns.why: Explaining mazloom he said 'long voice' for 'loud', and loud is sot 3aali.
patterns.english: not loud (not a loud voice)

patterns.title: mufrad (singular) for 'only / no sugar'
patterns.why: Answering 'with honey?' he said mufrad (singular / alone) to mean 'only, no sugar', and she had to guess mish sukkar.
patterns.english: mint tea with honey only, no sugar

patterns.title: 3ashaan (because) for 3an (about)
patterns.why: For 'I talked with her about my Arabic' he used 3ashaan (because / for the sake of), and 'about' is 3an.
patterns.english: I talked with my fiancee about my Arabic

patterns.title: far2 (difference, noun) for mukhtalef (different)
patterns.why: For 'why is it different' he used the noun far2 (difference), and the adjective is mukhtalef (3an).
patterns.english: why is it different from WhatsApp?

patterns.title: ta3aal (come here) said as a goodbye
patterns.why: Signing off he said ta3aal (come here) where a goodbye fits; may be a transcription slip.
patterns.english: bye

patterns.title: noa3 for 'kind of' (English calque; -> shwai)
patterns.why: For 'kind of cloudy' he used noa3 (type / kind), which does not mean 'somewhat'; her word for a bit is shwai.
patterns.english: and it's kind of cloudy

patterns.title: aktar for 'what else / what other' (-> shu kamaan / kelme taani)
patterns.why: For 'what else do I have' he calqued English 'what more' with aktar, and Levantine says shu kamaan or kelme taanye.
patterns.english: what else, what other word do I have?

patterns.title: baared (cold) where mbaare7 (yesterday) belongs
patterns.why: Retelling 'my AC broke yesterday' the word after khereb is baared (cold); baared and mbaare7 are near-homophones so this may be the engine.
patterns.english: my air conditioning broke yesterday

patterns.title: fata7 (open) for 7att (put), after her fix
patterns.why: A minute after her fix ma bit7utti he again said the 'open' verb for 'put' and she said mumtaz.
patterns.english: if you don't put it (in the fridge)

patterns.title: 3uzurti (non-word) for sorry (-> aasef)
patterns.why: Apologising for the audio he said 3uzurti, not a word, and her sorry is aasef (the engine may have mangled another word).
patterns.english: hi, sorry (about the audio)

patterns.title: 3ajool (MSA/Persian) for mista3jel (in a hurry)
patterns.why: For 'the customers were in a hurry' he used 3ajool, a different word not on her sheet; her word is mista3jel (plural mista3jileen).
patterns.english: the customers were in a hurry

patterns.title: bad7ak glossed as 'I smile' (we think 'I laugh'; her sheet lists both)
patterns.why: He glossed bad7ak as 'I smile' and we read it as 'I laugh' - but her own sheet row says 'i laugh / i smile', so she should say whether this counts at all.
patterns.english: I laugh / I make (someone) laugh

patterns.title: 'meetings' glossed as 'days off' (ijtimaa3aat vs 3utle)
patterns.why: Asked what the word in 'meetings make me bored' meant he said 'days off', and the word is meetings (the engine dropped the Arabic word, so details are uncertain).
patterns.english: meetings

patterns.title: The year 2026 said as alfein u sab3a 3eshreen (-> alfein u sitte u 3eshreen)
patterns.why: Giving the year he said seven where 2026 needs six and left out the u between the units and the tens (her pattern: alfein u 5amsa u 3eshrin).
patterns.english: two thousand twenty-six

patterns.title: zbayenna glossed as 'Arab customers' (-> our customers)
patterns.why: Glossing her sentence he read the -na ending of zbayenna as 'Arab', and it is 'our' (our customers).
patterns.english: it matters to us that our customers are happy

patterns.title: Invented plural el-3arabiin for 'the Arabs' (-> el-3arab)
patterns.why: For 'the Arabs' he built a plural el-3arabiin from 3arabi, and the plural is el-3arab.
patterns.english: the food is mainly for the Arabs

patterns.title: la sama7ti for law sama7ti (please, to a woman)
patterns.why: Three times he said la sama7ti for 'please', and the fixed phrase is law sama7ti (could be a vowel slip rather than a wrong word).
patterns.english: please (to a woman)

patterns.title: la- for 3ala ('a video on YouTube' said as video la YouTube)
patterns.why: 'On YouTube' takes 3ala; he used la- (for / of) and you let it pass.
patterns.english: I watched a video on YouTube.

patterns.title: Participle given a verb ending: inti mit2akti for inti mit2akkde (are you sure)
patterns.why: 'Are you (f) sure' is the feminine participle mit2akkde; he put the you-f verb ending -ti on it and you answered without fixing it.
patterns.english: Are you sure?

patterns.title: Listening: bey3asseb (makes angry) understood as 'is angry'
patterns.why: He glossed the make-angry verb bey3asseb as the state 'is angry' and you accepted with ممتاز (a minute earlier you also accepted 'what happened is sad' for بيزعل).
patterns.english: What you did is angering / makes people angry.

patterns.title: Singular 3andak for plural 3andkom (do you [all] have)
patterns.why: Asking Palestinians as a group with the singular 3andak; you let it pass here and fixed the same thing to ما عندكم a little later.
patterns.english: Don't you (pl) have an Iranian restaurant in Palestine?

patterns.title: el- on the comparative: el-akthar akel mufaddal for aktar akel mufaddal
patterns.why: 'The most preferred food' came out with el- on aktar (MSA-style el-akthar); Levantine keeps aktar bare before the noun. You said 'Mm' and moved on.
patterns.english: The most preferred food in the UAE is Iranian food.

patterns.title: malyaan (full) for 'busy' (mbaare7 malyaan kteer -> mbaare7 kaan mash8ool kteer)
patterns.wrong: mbaare7 malyaan kteer / kaan malyaan kteer
patterns.why: He called a busy day malyaan (full); we think a busy day is mash8ool, and your answer is missing from the recording here.
patterns.english: Yesterday was very busy.

patterns.title: abda2ek (I start you) for 'I'll send you' (-> ab3atlek)
patterns.why: He used bada (start) where he meant 'send you'; he caught it himself a moment later, but your line is missing from the recording.
patterns.english: I'm going to send you the link after the lesson.

patterns.title: musaa3ed (helper) for the noun 'help' (-> musaa3ada)
patterns.why: For 'more help' he first said musaa3ed (a helper) and asked which is right before landing on musaa3ada; your answer is missing from the recording.
patterns.english: The system needs more help.

patterns.title: Feminine adjective on a masculine noun (el-jaw ... m8ayyme -> el-jaw m8ayyem)
patterns.why: He described el-jaw (masculine) as m8ayyme; your sheet has 'el-jaw m8ayyem' but also 'it's cloudy = m8ayyme', so we need to know if m8ayyme is fine here.
patterns.english: The weather is hot and a bit cloudy.

patterns.title: el-usboo3 elli ba3do (the week after) for 'last week' (-> el-usboo3 elli faat)
patterns.why: He meant it started last week but said elli ba3do (the one after); you said 'What?' but gave no fix.
patterns.english: last week

patterns.title: MSA dual -aan for two hands (eedaan -> eedein)
patterns.why: In a list where he said ajrain and janayn with -ain, he gave 'two hands' as eedaan (MSA dual); you said eedein a minute later and let this one pass.
patterns.english: Hand, two hands.

patterns.title: bi- dropped before 'my body' (wala shee inkasar jismi 2abel -> wala shee inkasar bjismi 2abel)
patterns.why: After you prompted 'in my body' he said jismi with no bi- / fi in front, and you let it pass.
patterns.english: Nothing in my body broke before.

patterns.title: Invented plural eshyaat for 'things' (-> ashya)
patterns.why: He made the plural of eshi as eshyaat; you gave ashya as the plural a minute later on a different line.
patterns.english: I need to buy things.

patterns.title: Invented plural 3amaawem for 'uncles' (-> a3maam)
patterns.why: He made the plural of 3am as 3amaawem and you said mm-hmm; later in the lesson you said a3maami and a3maam.
patterns.english: three uncles

patterns.title: 'I brought' said as the she-form (jaabat -> jebet), even after her fix
patterns.why: For 'I brought' he says jaabat, which is 'she brought'; she had just corrected it to jebet and he said jaabat again.
patterns.english: I brought more...

patterns.title: hadol (these) used for 'those' (hadol el-fasateen -> hadoalaak el-fasateen)
patterns.why: He asked how to say 'those expensive dresses' and used hadol, which means 'these'; her sheet has hadoalaak for 'those' (her 'sa7' may have been about the el- only).
patterns.english: those expensive dresses

patterns.title: el- on a noun that already has an owner ending (el-madrasto -> madrasto)
patterns.why: He puts el- on a noun that already ends in his/my/your (madrasto), and a noun with an owner ending never takes el-; you said Mm-hmm and moved on.
patterns.english: the name of his old school

patterns.title: hadi (this, f) used with a masculine noun (hadi el-ma7al -> hada el-ma7al)
patterns.right: hada el-ma7al a7san ishi / hada a7san ma7al
patterns.why: Ma7al (store) is masculine, so 'this' should be hada, but he says hadi; you said 'it works' and only changed the sentence shape.
patterns.english: this store is the best

patterns.title: sabaa7 (from sabah el-kheir) used for 'in the morning' (el-saa3a wa7de sabaa7 -> el-sube7)
patterns.right: el-saa3a wa7de u taman da2aaye2 el-sube7
patterns.why: For 'in the morning' after a clock time he says sabaa7 (the greeting form) and we think the everyday word is el-sube7, as on her sheet; her chat simply left it out.
patterns.english: It's 1:08 in the morning

patterns.title: la- missing after mitshajje3 (motivated for): mshajje3 ed-dars -> mitshajje3 lad-dars
patterns.why: He puts the noun straight after the word for 'motivated' with no la- (and uses mshajje3, encouraging, for mitshajje3, encouraged); we think it needs la-, like mit7ammes la-.
patterns.english: I'm motivated for the lesson

patterns.title: a7san (best) said where he meant aswa2 (worst): a7san ez-zboon -> aswa2 zboon
patterns.why: Right after saying aswa2 twice he said a7san (best) in the same sentence, which flips the meaning; it looks like a slip of the tongue, and only the verb was fixed out loud.
patterns.english: The worst customer is the one who doesn't buy anything

patterns.title: Verb ta2akhar (he was late) where the adjective mit2akher (late) belongs (s7eet ta2akhar -> s7eet mit2akher)
patterns.why: He said 'I woke up' with the past verb ta2akhar (he was late) instead of the word mit2akher (late), which he had said a moment before.
patterns.english: I woke up late.

patterns.title: 3asha (dinner) said for 3ashra (ten) in a clock time (3ala el-3asha -> 3ala el-3ashra)
patterns.why: He said 3asha (dinner) when he meant 3ashra (ten) for the time, and her chat writes 3ala el-3ashara.
patterns.english: at ten o'clock

patterns.title: ma put in front of a positive statement (ma btjannen -> btjannen, 'is amazing')
patterns.why: He wanted to say the family is amazing but put ma in front, which turns it into 'is not amazing' (unless he meant ma as an exclamation or a filler).
patterns.english: this family is amazing

patterns.title: 'On Friday' said as bare jum3a (ana ra7 asaafer jum3a -> yoam el-jum3a)
patterns.why: He says the day as a bare jum3a with no yoam / el-; we think 'on Friday' needs yoam el-jum3a or el-jum3a.
patterns.english: I will travel on Friday.

patterns.title: Plural verb on a singular thing (jaa2u esh-shob -> ija esh-shob)
patterns.why: esh-shob (the heat) is one thing, so the verb should be ija, not the plural (MSA) jaa2u.
patterns.english: because the heat came

patterns.title: enno used for 'that / which' in a relative clause (ed-dars enno ... -> ed-dars elli ...)
patterns.why: He uses enno (the 'that' after say/know) to join a noun to its description, where we think elli belongs; he did it twice and she let it pass.
patterns.english: Let's do the lesson that you planned.

patterns.title: tafattatli (non-word) for 'you planned for me' (-> 5a66attili)
patterns.why: He made up a word for 'you planned for me'; she asked what he meant but never gave the word, so we think it should be 5a66attili (from her 5a66at).
patterns.english: the lesson that you planned for me

patterns.title: el- on a new thing after 'there is' (fi bil-lail el-2amar -> fi 2amar)
patterns.why: After fi (there is) the noun is new so it takes no el-; he first said it right, then switched to el-2amar and she only echoed 2amar.
patterns.english: In the sky at night there is a moon.

patterns.title: 'one' put before the noun (wa7de shams -> shams wa7de)
patterns.why: In Arabic 'one' comes after the noun like an adjective; he put it first and she said 'Great job'.
patterns.english: one sun

patterns.title: Verb after ra7 without its person prefix (ana ra7 3amelo -> ana ra7 a3melo)
patterns.why: After ra7 the verb still needs its person prefix (a- for I), and he said the bare stem after a pause; the a- may just be swallowed in the recording.
patterns.english: I'll do it, (with) a lot of mistakes
